blocks.text: Open source alternatives to Ionic Enterprise Plugins

Move from closed enterprise-only plugins to Capgo's open source Capacitor stack. Use the plugins before you pay, add support when it becomes critical, and use Builder when native builds are part of the migration.
Why Capgo is different from an enterprise plugin contract

Ionic Enterprise plugins are sold as a commercial package. Capgo takes a different path: the plugins are open source, the migration guides are public, and paid help is
            there when your team needs guaranteed response times, expert migration work, or native build capacity.

Capgo-maintained plugins are visible, auditable, and forkable. You can inspect the native code, patch it, or keep control if your security team asks what ships in the
              app.

You do not need a paid enterprise contract just to try the plugins. Pay when it is critical: migration help, guaranteed support, governance, or business-critical
              delivery.

The directory covers 154+ plugins across auth, storage, payments, MDM, analytics, device APIs, native UI, and live updates. Start from the exact native capability
              you need, not a bundle.

When a migration touches native projects, Capgo Builder can produce iOS and Android builds with logs, signing, and store-ready artifacts instead of leaving CI work to
              your team.
Open source plugin code, public docs, and the option to fork or self-maintain if your policy requires it.
Commercial packages where access and fixes depend on the vendor relationship.
Use the plugin stack first. Pay for support, migration, enterprise guarantees, or native build capacity when those become important.
Enterprise value is commonly tied to a paid contract before teams can standardize on the package.
Capgo pairs plugins with live updates and Builder, so teams can migrate code and still produce signed native builds.
Plugin licensing and CI/build delivery are often separate decisions.
Capgo does not ship an Ionic Portals or App Federation replacement yet. We focus on plugins, live updates, native builds, and custom native gaps.
If your main requirement is embedding multiple mini-apps in one native shell, keep evaluating dedicated portal or federation tools.
Start with the direct replacements, then decide where you need support, migration help, or Capgo Builder for native delivery.
Credentials saved with biometric access control can be read only after the native biometric prompt.
Native Biometric covers the full credential-vault flow

It is not only a biometric prompt. Store access and refresh tokens in the native Keychain or Keystore with biometric access control. The platform requires biometrics
              before your app can read them, while your app decides when to request the protected read.
Save, retrieve, check, and delete the tokens or credentials your app needs.
Protect credential reads with Face ID, Touch ID, or Android biometrics.
Request a protected read when your app resumes, after a timeout, or before a sensitive area.

For separate iOS prompts, verifyIdentity supports device-passcode fallback. Choose whether enrollment changes invalidate protected credentials; protected reads stay
                biometric-only.

Capgo is not trying to clone every Ionic enterprise product. It is the practical path when you need open source native plugins, live updates, native builds, and
              direct help for app-specific native gaps.
